commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[iac] Temporarily allow deleting 17 CoreWeave hero checkpoints (#11137)

Replace the `marin/grug/hero-*` delete deny on `marin-us-east-02a` with
71 protected path globs so that 17 superseded hero checkpoint
directories can be removed from 02A after they are copied to
`s3://marin-us-east-01a` under the same keys. This frees 72.96 TB
(425,066 objects) in the 02A zone, which was at 948.9 of 1000.6 TB on
2026-11-09. `marin-us-east-01a` is ad hoc storage in zone US-EAST-01A
(100 TiB quota) outside the `marin-buckets` stack; how long it will be
kept is not decided.

Deletable step directories, under
`marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/<run>/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/`:

| Run | Steps | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| hero-ctx65k-step372k | 385500 through 390000, every 500 (10) | Inputs
to `hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251`, which is saved
and is the current handoff |
| hero-lce-global184-step390k | 390500, 391000, 391500, 392000, 392500,
393000, 393491 (all 7) | The Global 1.84 262K finalist; #8435 chose log
floor 65536² |

hero-ctx65k-step372k keeps 378000, 384000 and 390251 (the GB200 canary
checkpoint), plus its executor and tracker files. Every other hero-* run
that existed on 2026-11-09 (64 runs) stays fully protected, including
the merged handoff and the log floor 65536² finalist. #10218 left
non-lineage hero-* runs unprotected; this list covers them. hero-* runs
created while this is applied are not protected.

Checked against a listing of all 2,318,740 objects under
`marin/grug/hero-*` taken 2026-11-09: the new deny leaves exactly the
manifest's 425,066 objects undenied. Manifest sha256
`c0244dc53b624cbb05aa0158bcadb8e3f05cd2ad84459453fe9cd18631b52db9`, one
`marin/grug/<run>/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-N` per line, in table
order. Each directory is a self-contained OCDBT checkpoint, so
whole-directory copies restore from their new path and deleting whole
directories leaves no dangling references. The archive copy is a plain
recursive copy. Before any 02A delete, every key and size under the 17
archived directories must match the 2026-11-09 listing of the source.
Versioning is suspended on 02A, so the deletion there is permanent.

Sequence: merge; copy all 17 directories and check them against the
listing; only then an operator posts the credentialed preview and
applies it; delete exactly the manifest prefixes from 02A; then revert
this change to restore the wildcard deny by 2026-11-13. #10245 applied
its revert with a targeted `pulumi up --target` on the 02a bucket policy
resource; check the preview for unrelated drift before a plain `up`.

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[inference] Add an optional Parallel web search tool to the dashboard (#11068)

The serve dashboard can give the model a `web_search` tool backed by
Parallel's search API. The tool exists only when the serving process
holds a
Parallel API key. Then `/info` reports `web_search: true`, the Chat view
shows
a Web search checkbox, and `POST /web-search` forwards each call to
Parallel
`/v1/search`.

The key stays on the server. It reaches the job as the Iris secret
`PARALLEL_API_KEY`, which `parallel_web_search_from_secret()` reads in
`_register_dashboard`. `marin-serve iris` gains `--secret NAME SOURCE`,
the
form `iris job run` uses, so
`--secret PARALLEL_API_KEY env:PARALLEL_API_KEY` resolves the reference
on the
client and attaches the value to the job, not to the job command. A
launcher
that calls `build_dashboard_app` directly must submit the same secret
and pass
`web_search=parallel_web_search_from_secret()`. Inference jobs submitted
from
a serving task get its other forwarded secrets as an explicit map
without
`PARALLEL_API_KEY`, because they may run remote model code. In direct
mode the
model server shares the dashboard's task and can read the key file.

The route validates `objective` and `search_queries` with a Pydantic
model and
drops other fields, so a holder of the capability URL cannot select
other
Parallel options. Invalid arguments return 422 without a Parallel call.
Parallel's status and body are returned unchanged, and the browser gives
any
error body to the model. A transport failure returns 502 without a
retry. A
live search returned 10 results, about 11 KB, in 2.3 s.

`/info` adds `web_search` next to the `ServingInfo` fields because the
dashboard app owns the route. A `ServingInfo` field would make each
caller keep
the flag and the `web_search` argument in agreement.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[ops] Keep CoreWeave runtime logs off the root filesystem (#11079)

Redirect CoreWeave shim and gVisor logs to
`/mnt/local/iris-runtime/runsc` when the Iris node-agent DaemonSet
starts. An init container preserves provider runtime options and backs
up the configuration before replacing it atomically. Replacement nodes
get the same setup automatically. Existing shims keep their original
destinations; historical log cleanup remains an operator action.

Publish root and `/tmp` filesystem gauges and alert below 5% free for
five minutes, independently of the NVMe cache gauge. Deploy the updated
node agents and Grafana to enable the fix and alert. Task and Shellbox
sandbox `/tmp` already use private disk-backed Kubernetes storage.

Shorten `OPS.md` to common commands and pointers, with detailed runbooks
in focused reference pages and incident evidence in
[Echo](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/947).

Part of #11075.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Score fixed references with the serving policy (#10614)

Score fixed, pretokenized references through the trainer evaluation
callback, after serving weights are synchronized. Emit NLL averaged
within each example and then across examples, alongside token-weighted
NLL by domain, plus per-step JSONL with exact token IDs, answer-start
token offsets, and chosen-token log probabilities.

Missing or misaligned scores fail that step's scoring rather than
logging a wrong value. Because this is a diagnostic, the failure logs a
warning, omits the step's metrics and JSONL, and training continues. To
support that, the trainer now applies each callback's `error_behavior`
to `collect_evaluation`, which it previously awaited directly; the
existing evaluation callbacks use `RAISE` and still fail the run.

NLL is a distribution diagnostic, not a generated-answer correctness
metric. This callback does not select checkpoints, enforce preservation
thresholds, or stop training. The CPU cases run in the skyrl-wheel CI
job.

Also give the `test_iris_monitor.py` sequential-child fixture a running
task. Since #10909 the monitor requires one before it drops the queue
deadline, so the test from #10860 failed on main whenever CI selected
`tests/ci`.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Make the log-scaled 262K run the hero's recipe and current run (#11044)

Make log floor 65536 squared the hero's 262K recipe and
`hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k` the current hero run. `HERO_MODEL` drops
`qk_mult_long_scale=1.108` (global 1.84) and scales each global-layer
query that sees `n` keys in its document by `(1 + 0.1 ln(n/65536))^2`,
up to 1.296 at 262K. `CURRENT_HERO_RUN_ID` names the log run, so
`hero_checkpoint_paths()` and `trigger_hero.sh` now follow its lineage.

The run trained from launch commit `0454bdd609`, tagged
`hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`, and ended at
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491`,
the starting point for downstream training. The training config built at
this head matches the one built at `0454bdd609`. Against the global 1.84
run at step 393491, the clean macro at 262K tied (1.6434 vs 1.6433), and
MRCR full-context NLL fell from 0.0252 to 0.0223 (Holm p < .001 at all 7
checkpoints). Each recipe has one seed. See the [#8435
result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6748198431),
[W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k),
and [marin-logbooks
#37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37).

- The vLLM and CPU exporters and the Hugging Face upload refuse log
scaling, so they cannot convert this run's checkpoints yet. The README
says so.
- The vibe check samples at 4K context with the native model, below the
floor, so its output does not change.
- The daily hero canary trains the recipe from step 390251, so it
switches from global 1.84 to log scaling.
- Unset log scaling options in `launch_diagnostics.py` keep the hero's
values, so `--no-log-scaling` turns log scaling off for a control arm
such as global 1.84.

Part of #8435

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Make the hero log scaling slope required and add a power (#10986)

Replace the fixed slope of the hero's log scaling with a required
`log_scaling_alpha` field on `GrugModelConfig`, and add a
`log_scaling_power` field that defaults to 1. `launch_diagnostics.py`
gets `--log-scaling-alpha` and `--log-scaling-power`. The factor is now
`(1 + alpha * ln(max(n / n_floor, 1))) ** power`. Setting only one of
the floor and the slope raises `ValueError`, as does a power other than
1 without a floor, and there is no default slope.

#10923 added the optional scaling with `LOG_SCALING_ALPHA = 0.1`, the
value in Inkling's released configs, where it is paired with a floor of
128000. The same coefficient sets the hero's YaRN-style QK schedule.
Neither source tested that slope at the hero's floors or at 262K, and a
slope other than 0.1 could not launch without a config value. The field
uses Inkling's name but has no default, so a run that enables log
scaling must state its slope.

The power lets a run square the factor: floor 65536, slope 0.1 and power
2 give 1.296 at the end of a 262K document. At power 1 the code skips
the pow.

There is no effect with log scaling off, which remains the default.
Against the code before this PR on CPU, a tiny model's logits were
bitwise equal with scaling off and with slope 0.1 at the default power,
and so were factors at floor 65536. `to_hf_config` still refuses log
scaling, so exports and upload still raise, and SkyRL behavior does not
change. No hero constant changes.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris] Prefer the image's Python in the default task setup (#11017)

Set `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=system` on the default setup's `uv sync`, so a
task venv uses the image's `/usr/local/bin/python3.12` when it matches
the requested version. uv's default preference chose any managed 3.12
build in the node-local `/uv/cache/python` first. Nodes on `cw-rno2a`
had cached different builds. Older python-build-standalone builds lack
`os.pidfd_open` and `signal.pidfd_send_signal`; upstream fixed this in
astral-sh/python-build-standalone#1163. Three of four workers of
`/rav/agentic-drafts-ramp-4` failed in Shellbox's `LocalMachineFactory`
on such a build.

On one `cw-rno2a` node, 8 tasks with the default preference ran the
cached managed 3.12.13, which lacks both APIs. 8 tasks with
`UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=system` ran the image's 3.12.16, which has both.
uv still uses a managed build when the image has no matching Python.

The setting is part of the client-rendered setup script, so it applies
to jobs submitted from this revision and to their children without an
Iris rollout.

Incident: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/937

Fixes #11014

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <1419010+ravwojdyla@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[datakit] Read the Tier 3 ferry input from normalized Nemotron-CC (#11098)

The Tier 3 Datakit ferry now reads the normalized Nemotron-CC v1
`hq_actual` split at
`gs://marin-eu-west4/normalized/nemotron_v1/hq_actual_d6502d2c` and
normalizes it again. It read the raw Common Crawl dump at
`gs://marin-eu-west4/raw/nemotro-cc-eeb783` before. That dump is gone:
its prefix holds only the `.executor_info` and `.executor_status` that
the failed run wrote. The `raw/` prefix is also gone from us-central1,
us-central2, us-east1, and us-east5, and soft delete is off, so GCS
cannot restore it. Who deleted it is unknown. The [2026-11-09
run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42578325577)
failed at its input check.

The last good raw-input run (2026-10-26) normalized 1,000 `kind=actual`
files, 301M documents, into 1,382 shards. Normalize hash-partitions by
document ID, so each `hq_actual` file is a uniform sample of the split,
at about 188K documents per file. `FERRY_TEST_MAX_FILES=1600` selects
about 301M documents (655 GB). A 448 MiB partition target gives about
1,390 shards of 216K documents. The normalize step reads `source_id`
(the WARC record ID) as its ID field, so its output columns match the
raw-input runs. Before the DAG starts, the ferry checks the split's
`SUCCESS` status and Parquet files. The input step is then a cache hit,
so StepRunner writes nothing into the split's directory, which other
pipelines also read.

An Iris job in europe-west4 ran the input and normalize steps with
`FERRY_TEST_MAX_FILES=4`. The input step was a cache hit, and normalize
wrote 753K unique records to 3 shards with the expected columns at a
peak worker memory of 3.7 GB. The full DAG has not run on this input
yet; the next weekly run is the first.

Incident record: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/955

Fixes #11096

[tests] Move misplaced tests to the packages they cover (#10993)

Move tests that live in one package but only test another package's code
into the package they test, and delete the copies that duplicate tests
already there, so each behavior is tested once in the place its owners
look.

The shard-cache consolidation tests in
tests/test_consolidate_metadata.py exercised only Levanter, so they now
live in lib/levanter/tests/test_shard_cache_consolidation.py; its
relative_shard tests were dropped because test_new_cache.py's
relative_shard_path tests already cover them, with two new parametrize
rows for the cases they missed (a doubled separator on the output-path
side and a local sibling path). The loopback-trust unit tests of
rigging.server_auth move from lib/iris/tests/test_auth.py to
lib/rigging/tests/test_server_auth.py, leaving Iris with its controller
integration tests.

Duplicates were removed rather than moved: Iris's loopback-admin and
tokenless-rejection resolve_auth tests (covered by rigging's
test_resolve_auth_loopback_admin_when_no_assertion and
test_resolve_auth_rejects_tokenless_without_assertion), and fray's
wrap_multiprocess GPU-validation tests (covered by Iris's
test_build_multigpu_hook_requires_gpu and _requires_divisible_gpu_count,
which fray delegates to). The helper module tests/test_utils.py is
replaced by tests/vllm/tpu_availability.py, holding skip_if_no_tpu for
its two vLLM importers; its unused check_load_config and
skip_if_module_missing are deleted.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[haliax] Index NamedRef with Python integer lists (#10978)

Reading or writing a NamedRef with a Python list of indices, such as
`ref[{"x": [2, 4]}]` or a list selector on a sliced view, now selects
those positions. Before, every such call failed with `ValueError: too
many values to unpack`.

The combined list went straight into the `jax.Ref` index tuple, and JAX
reads a Python list there as several separate indices. Combining a list
with the view's prefix now produces an int32 `NamedArray` on the indexed
axis, after the same bounds checks and negative-index handling, so the
result keeps that axis as list indexing of a `NamedArray` does. A bare
index array would instead take the name of any other axis of the same
length and read or write the wrong elements on a multi-axis ref. The
list-index test that #10883 marked as an expected failure now passes,
and new tests cover direct list reads and writes, including a list whose
length equals another axis's size.

Only `lib/haliax/tests/test_named_ref.py` was run locally; CI covers the
rest of the Haliax and Levanter suites.

---------

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Surface declared counts and independent QC in the Atlas (#10924)

Inventory-only campaign-release rows in the RL Data Atlas showed no
example count, no curriculum area, and only *Not assessed*: the
curriculum release carries sources with curated outputs, and no field
existed for the QC a pinned release performed on itself.

Publication now joins inventory declarations with a pinned row count as
*declared*-basis source rows. Release totals, placement statistics and
the processed-examples summary stay matched-only, so declared rows count
without claiming curriculum placement. Re-running `--corpus` merges
current dataset declarations over the recorded inventory, so a refreshed
release picks up new or edited declarations without re-curation; the
inventory build also dedupes by declaration ID, which the merge made
observable.

`SourceInfo` gains a typed `independent_qc` block — verdict, method,
reviewed and admitted counts, pinned evidence URL — that projects into
the catalog declaration and reaches the UI unchanged through the loader
and sources API. The Atlas lists it under its own **Independent QC**
column and detail section, beside and distinct from the sampled curation
grade. The five Smartie campaign releases state their manifests' facts:
the SWE-Smith cohort reports *good* with 8,045 reviewed and admitted on
Daytona-oracle and Good-verdict retention, the repaired shared
environment reports *good* with 324 admitted of 2,205 reviewed, the
CalibForge admitted cohort reports *some issues* (oracle skipped,
publication pending), and the staged archives report their reviewed
counts and verification limits without an admitted claim.

To surface the counts and QC after merge: publish a fresh curriculum
release from the completed campaign corpus (`driver --corpus
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/campaigns/campaign-releases-2026.11-04-9/corpus.json
--embed coverage` with the campaign's pool flags), load it with
`load_curriculum.py`, and rerun the Atlas loader after the declaration
edit reaches production (a metadata-only campaign selecting the five
sources republishes them). The app needs a Marina release for the UI
change.
